title: How simple words become a graph
narration: Let's see how Digital Brain turns a short library note into a graph, using simple phases and a repeatable run of our project.

title: Read a short note
narration: The library app uses a book list. A help guide explains the app. The book list is a small data store. These notes provide evidence.

title: Find the document parts
narration: Mark It Down reads uploaded files. Python finds documents and sections. Each item becomes a node; a connection is an edge. Meaning links come later.

title: Connect the key items
narration: Optional OpenAI or Claude enrichment finds key items: library app and book list. It proposes their uses connection, item types, source identifier, and exact quote. Similar connection words get one standard label.

title: Check the quoted words
narration: The server checks the quote, named items, and allowed types. An invented toy-list quote is rejected because it is absent from the note. These filters reduce errors; they do not prove every interpretation.

title: Keep one item; keep its source
narration: Both notes refer to one library app, so matching names are merged. Every connection keeps its source, quote, and content fingerprint to detect later changes.

title: See the real builder output
narration: Our actual builder run accepts two meaning links, merges the shared app, and rejects the invented quote. AI proposals are controlled here; no live model call is made.

title: Save and review
narration: Django saves a numbered draft. Review quality and evidence. Graphify groups existing connected nodes using Network X and Leiden clustering; it does not invent facts.

title: Publish the reviewed version
narration: A person publishes the reviewed graph. Answers check current evidence and viewer access. Restricted sources stay outside AI.

title: Read. Find. Connect. Check.
narration: A graph connects useful items and keeps their original evidence. AI suggests links. The application checks them. A person reviews and publishes.
